summary:
COSMOS – Explore the Universe, Your Way

Cosmos started with a simple thought: what if learning about space wasn't just about reading books or looking at pictures, but actually exploring and creating things yourself?

We built Cosmos to make space exploration more fun, interactive, and accessible. It allows users to explore the universe, discover celestial objects, and create their own planets and solar systems using our Cosmic Builder. Instead of just learning about how the universe works, users get the opportunity to experiment and experience it in their own way.

We wanted to make something that could bring space science closer to everyone, especially students who are curious about what lies beyond Earth. Cosmos aims to turn complex ideas about the universe into an experience that is easier to understand and exciting to explore.

For us, Cosmos is more than just a project. It's an attempt to turn curiosity into exploration and make people feel a little closer to the universe.
details:
I created Cosmos because I felt that exploring space should be more than just looking at pictures or reading facts in a textbook. I wanted people to actually experience the feeling of exploring the universe.

Cosmos is a web-based platform where users can explore space, discover celestial objects, and even create their own planets and solar systems. I built different experiences, including Cosmos Explorer, Universe View, and Cosmic Builder, to make learning about space more interactive. With Cosmic Builder, users can bring their imagination to life by creating their own worlds.

I hope Cosmos makes astronomy easier and more interesting for students and anyone who has ever looked at the night sky and wondered what's out there. Not everyone gets the opportunity to experience space science beyond books, and I wanted to make that experience more accessible.

I used React and Three.js to build the platform and its interactive 3D environment. I also used Google AI Studio during development to help bring my ideas to life.

What makes Cosmos special to me is that users don't just explore a universe created by someone else; they also get to create their own. While building it, I focused on making the experience visually engaging, easy to navigate, and enjoyable even for someone who knows very little about astronomy.

At the end of the day, I want Cosmos to make people more curious about space. Because sometimes, one small question about the universe can lead to something much bigger.
